rows.title: A trivial Bash call waited on the full work of the heavy Bash hooks
rows.note: The llm-legs half of the same pour is llm-legs@c85ff90 (instruction-write-gate read-only note, worker-launch-gate early exit, instruction-files batched realpath).

rows.title: context-nudge read a 1 MiB transcript tail through jq on every tool call
rows.note: Design §4: 79 ms a call before the 64 KiB tail read, 62 ms after; its own tail read cut it, not the fast path.

rows.title: An Edit or Write waits over 500 ms on hooks: edit-conflict-notice before, commit-journal after
rows.note: Design §7.1 calibration: 655 ms on 2026-09-29; 549 ms in the live run of 2026-09-29 21:18. 2026-09-30: 768 ms p50 = edit-conflict-notice 390 ms before + commit-journal 280 / instruction-watch check 237 ms after. The before side was live_run_holder forking head, sed and a same_owner subshell per unswept worker-run record of every repository (46 records); it now reads them with builtins and asks same_owner only of a record that concerns the file. The after side is the hooks run of the same night (hook_every_call / hook_grows_* on commit-journal and instruction-watch check); see the handoff.

rows.title: A non-trivial Bash call waits over 500 ms on hooks
rows.note: 2026-09-30 03:18: 867 ms p50 over 346 calls = review-flow-gate 253 ms (p90 841) before + commit-journal 178 / instruction-watch check 170 ms (p90 843 / 344) after; every other hook ends under 180 ms. All three hooks are the problems of the night's hooks run, so this run changed none of them.

rows.title: The inline SessionStart branch-slug check has no hook-time line
rows.note: An inline one-liner in settings.json cannot source hook-time.sh; one git call per chat start. The ident is the sha1 of the exact command, so any edit to it is judged again.

rows.title: suites · llm-legs doubles its wall clock when several full runs share the machine
rows.note: Narrowed to concurrent full runs: the 1326 s run of 2026-09-30 02:29 local overlapped three other full llm-legs runs (02:24 2060 s, 02:38 1538 s, 02:39 1463 s; logdirs under $TMPDIR/run-suites.*), each -j 5 on 10 cores. Its summed suite time was 6506 s against about 2200 s in quiet runs, and wall ≈ summed/5, so the run was throughput-bound; no suite regressed. The design accepts it: run-suites has no cross-invocation lock, and handoff 2026-09-28 §4 forbids a cross-chat queue. A slow run with no overlapping full run is a new cause for this row.

rows.title: Unaccounted CPU is the fork and exec cost of parallel test suites and statusline renders
rows.note: 60 s process census 2026-09-30 03:25-03:31: 1 081 new processes a second; test suites 61 % (four night worktrees in run-suites at once), statusline 20 % (5 sessions), hooks 8.5 %, worker-run 5.8 %, review-bench 3.8 %. The statusline share is item 2 of docs/handoffs/2026-09-28-harness-performance-fix.md.

rows.title: The tripwire journaled writes another record already carried, so one write counted as growth twice
rows.note: Event 5751c770d8700227 (2026-09-29T20:50:18Z, compaction SessionStart of a session whose own baseline dated from before 2026-09-28T19:43Z) listed 20 files: 15 synced-skill files and hammerspoon/CLAUDE.md whose alert marks earlier checks had claimed (20:14-20:33Z, 09:39Z), and review-tiers.md whose 2026-09-28T19:43Z record had outlived its one-day mark. alert_once now journals only the files this check claimed, and a mark lives past the baselines' week-old sweep.

rows.title: Claude Code org-skill sync writes ~/.claude/skills/synced, which no gate can see
rows.note: Narrowed to one cause: 2026-09-29 20:14/20:20/20:33Z the harness itself synced the newly published org skill google-workspace (SKILL.md + references/*.md, 13-47 kB each) into the three synced/<org>_<account>/ dirs beside manifest.json and .last-complete-round; the dir is gitignored in claude-setup and written by no tool call. Dismissal proposed in the handoff.

rows.title: Ad-hoc hook profiling fed synthetic session ids to the live tripwire
rows.note: Narrowed to one cause: every baseline-missing record since 2026-09-28T23:00Z names a sid no chat owns (perf-big-93348, perf-big-8746, perf-lvb, hlprof-a): check runs with made-up session ids against ~/.cache/claude-instruction-watch rather than INSTRUCTION_WATCH_STATE. No committed code or transcript names those ids. A real chat losing its baseline would match this row too, so it stays open.

rows.title: Background work that never ends held every end-of-turn ask for hours: a Storybook server, a night-job Monitor, agents launched one after another (35 h in one chat)
rows.note: stop-dispatch.sh holds asks for background work at most STOP_DISPATCH_HELD_CAP (3600 s), then runs them at that stop with busy empty and the journal line's `held` naming what it would have called busy, and the hold restarts; ask-span-drill stays silent under STOP_HELD; ask-run-unfinished also sees waiter tasks under the 2.1.285 label `subagent`. The doctor's ask-busy rule does not see asks run under `held`, by design.

rows.title: A half-read joined notice was never asked for: its turn's stops were all busy, and ask-word-reading read only the current turn at the next idle stop
rows.note: words_journal.py ask reads every turn since the last stop it ran at (reading-checked), asks once per notice (asked-reading), and a reading written for a late ask settles the old row ok (reading-late) instead of reading as unprompted (asked). Evidence: words:1790697197/4ba97859, turn 9, only commit+push read; next idle stop 16:44Z was turn 12+.

blind_spots.what: interpreter start before a hook's first line
blind_spots.reason: hook-time.sh times the body only: about 4 ms for /bin/bash, about 11 ms for Homebrew bash 5
blind_spots.would_catch_if: the harness reported each hook's spawn-to-exit time

blind_spots.what: MCP server start-up, worker spawn and relay latency
blind_spots.reason: no journal line from the MCP servers, worker-run spawn or the relay
blind_spots.would_catch_if: worker-run and the relay wrote start and ready stamps to a journal this doctor reads

blind_spots.what: worker-run supervise loops, worker-pick, review-cell preparation
blind_spots.reason: they run outside any hook and write no timing
blind_spots.would_catch_if: each wrote its elapsed time to the hook journal under its own key

blind_spots.what: launchd jobs; Hammerspoon's own tasks other than the menu builds
blind_spots.reason: only the menu builds write a journal line
blind_spots.would_catch_if: each LaunchAgent wrapper in ~/.local/libexec wrote its run time to a journal

blind_spots.what: calls from sessions outside bypassPermissions (who h)
blind_spots.reason: their wait includes the human answering a permission prompt, so every wait and floor leaves them out
blind_spots.would_catch_if: the transcript marked when the permission answer arrived, so the hook part could be split off

blind_spots.what: hook output that reached a spool file instead of its reader
blind_spots.reason: 5 of 4 561 folded review-flow-gate runs on 2026-09-29 carried STATUS=… LINES=… between key and exit; the reader tolerates it
blind_spots.would_catch_if: the fold counted spool files with extra lines and judged that count

blind_spots.what: the 13-15 % of tool batches the time join cannot tie to a call
blind_spots.reason: hook batches join calls by time only
blind_spots.would_catch_if: hook-time's line carried the tool_use_id (contract row da)

blind_spots.what: suite runs missing from test-history.jsonl, so suites_at_once and test_slow see only part of the load
blind_spots.reason: bin/statusline-work-probe.sh writes a row only when a render of the owning chat sees the run start and end within 15 s; 3 of 4 full llm-legs runs overlapping 2026-09-30 02:24-03:03 local left no row
blind_spots.would_catch_if: share/run-suites.sh appended its own wall time, outcome and overlap to the journal at exit

blind_spots.what: which process trees the unaccounted CPU of load:unseen belongs to
blind_spots.reason: the sampler counts new pids machine-wide and never their ancestry, so Load cannot tell test suites from statusline renders or hooks
blind_spots.would_catch_if: the sampler polled the pid list through its 2 s window and counted new processes per origin (test suite, statusline, hook, worker-run, review-bench) from each one's ancestor chain

blind_spots.what: test suites run by headless workers and night fixers
blind_spots.reason: `tests running` and test-history come from statusline work probes, and a `claude -p` session renders no statusline: 03:19 sampled 0 while four night worktrees ran run-suites
blind_spots.would_catch_if: run-suites.sh wrote a start and end line per suite to a journal this doctor reads

blind_spots.what: one instruction-file write journaled by two tripwire records
blind_spots.reason: the guards rule counts each record per file; a record carries no write key (hash@mtime), so a second record of the same write reads as new growth
blind_spots.would_catch_if: each events.jsonl file entry carried its alert key and the guards rule counted a key once

blind_spots.what: the background task type labels Stop hooks filter the payload on
blind_spots.reason: Claude Code 2.1.285 labels an Agent task `subagent` where ask-run-unfinished.sh matched only `local_agent`; the stop journal records the count of live tasks, never their types
blind_spots.would_catch_if: the stop journal recorded each live background task's type, so a hook filter matching none of the labels in use showed
